How many iterations are performed for this loop, and how often?

For very large loops, I believe `for..of` is still slower than `for (let i = 0; ...`. Since this could be running every frame, we do need to consider the performance.

References:
- https://dev.to/maafaishal/benchmarking-for-while-forof-and-arrayforeach-using-performancenow-1jjg
- https://waspdev.com/articles/2026-01-01/javascript-for-of-loops-are-actually-fast

In both cases, note the different conclusions depending on the number of iterations.
Can we add a little context in an inline comment? Why do values outside the clamp min/max not make sense? Why do we need to clamp? how would the values go out of range?
This is going to use a spherical approximation and not the true ellipsoid circumference. Is that adequate for the use case here, or should the true circumference be used?

Just curious—What's the motivation on mocking this? Is the `TerrainPicker` difficult to construct or is there another source of friction? 

Generally speaking, it'd preferable to call through this function call, even if you are spying on it. (Though this doesn't need to prevent this PR from being merged—Just adding the unit test is already an improvement.)

While calculating a value rather than hardcoding it can make tests more resilient, in this case the function computing the expected value is part of the [system under test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System_under_test). Depending on it may lead to cases where there's a bug somewhere in `TerrainMesh` but this unit test still passes. I'd opt to hard code it, or compute it outside of `TerrainMesh` operations.

(Again, this doesn't need to prevent this PR from being merged—Just adding the unit test is already an improvement.)

How many iterations are performed for this loop, and how often?

For very large loops, I believe `for..of` is still slower than `for (let i = 0; ...`. Since this could be running every frame, we do need to consider the performance.

References:
- https://dev.to/maafaishal/benchmarking-for-while-forof-and-arrayforeach-using-performancenow-1jjg
- https://waspdev.com/articles/2026-01-01/javascript-for-of-loops-are-actually-fast

In both cases, note the different conclusions depending on the number of iterations.
As above, how many tiles are in this list? If it's a "small" number, then `for..of` is probably ok.

Minor naming nit: we usually use "scratch" to describe some pre-allocated memory that will be overwritten repeatedly (rather than re-allocating it each time). In this case, I think the clamp min/max values stay constant? So simply `const clampMaximum` would be clearer.
Can we add a little context in an inline comment? Why do values outside the clamp min/max not make sense? Why do we need to clamp? how would the values go out of range?
Always good to see more specs!
